alternatives.root_cause: Quote service became unreachable or slow on its own
alternatives.why_not: Quote had no changes and answered in well under a millisecond in sampled traces; the breakage tracks shipping's address edits, not quote's health.

alternatives.root_cause: Checkout broke and its PlaceOrder path began erroring
alternatives.why_not: Checkout's error change points trail each shipping QUOTE_ADDR edit, and its other dependencies (cart, payment, currency, product-catalog) stayed fast and clean.

alternatives.root_cause: A wrong artifact was rolled out to shipping
alternatives.why_not: The change record is an environment variable update, not an image or version change; the running artifact was never altered.

verdict.summary: Shipping's QUOTE_ADDR environment value was set to a non-existent quote endpoint (quote-gone:8090), so shipping's quote calls fail and checkout's PlaceOrder errors follow.
verdict.reasoning: Shipping went from a zero baseline to a high, bursty error ratio (tr_13b32e15839f) and the change log shows the QUOTE_ADDR variable on shipping pointed at a host that does not exist, applied at 12:17:34, reverted at 12:23:06, and re-applied at 12:35:49 (tr_70bc73ff8a82). Checkout's error ratio has two change points, 12:19:16 and 12:37:16, each trailing one of those edits (tr_70e3e8221538) — exactly the propagation pattern expected if shipping is the broken hop and checkout is merely the caller that noticed. Quote had no changes of its own (tr_82f9f7338102), and in sampled traces quote responds in sub-millisecond time when it is reached (tr_f893ec68e8fb), so the dependency is healthy and it is the address value itself that is wrong. Failures are fast rather than hanging, which rules out freeze/partition/latency classes.
open_questions: Shipping and checkout logs were empty over the window, so the exact failure text (name resolution vs connection refused) was not confirmed
The error-ratio series for shipping showed no sustained departure flag, so the precise per-edit onset timestamps on shipping were not pinned
Whether the second application at 12:35:49 was intentional automation or a faulty rollback loop
